questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Which of the following is something owls do NOT have?
A. Spherical eyeballs
B. Hearing
C. A complete digestive tract
Answer: A. Unlike many other animals, owls have eye tubes that are fixed directly in their sockets, which allows for excellent depth perception and a wide field of view. However, as a result, they cannot move their eyes. To compensate, owls have incredibly flexible necks and can rotate their heads up to 270 degrees in either direction.
questions.de: Welche Form haben die Augen von Eulen statt kugelförmiger Augäpfel, sodass sie fest in den Höhlen sitzen und nicht bewegt werden können?
questions.en: Instead of spherical eyeballs, what shape are owls' eyes, fixed in their sockets so that the birds cannot move them?

timeline.labelEn: Paleocene fossils show owls already existing as a distinct bird lineage
timeline.labelDe: Fossilien aus dem Paläozän zeigen, dass Eulen bereits eine eigene Vogellinie bildeten

questions.notes: Card correct: an owl's large eye in a small skull has become tubular, fixed in sclerotic tubes, so owls cannot move their eyes and instead turn their heads up to 270° (Wikipedia: Owl). Asked as the positive fact behind the 'NOT' question. Timeline: Paleocene owl genera Berruornis and Ogygoptynx, 60–57 Mya (same page).

questions.cardText:
[Earth Science] What is the largest desert in the world?
A. Antarctica B. Siberia C. Sahara
Answer: A. Despite being a desert, Antarctica holds about 70% of the world’s freshwater locked up as ice.
questions.de: Welche Polarwüste, die rund 70 % des Süßwassers der Erde als Eis speichert, ist die größte Wüste der Welt?
questions.en: Which polar desert, holding about 70% of the world's fresh water as ice, is the largest desert in the world?

timeline.labelEn: Antarctica's ice shelf is first sighted, by Bellingshausen's Russian expedition and by Edward Bransfield
timeline.labelDe: Das Schelfeis der Antarktis wird erstmals gesichtet – von Bellingshausens russischer Expedition und von Edward Bransfield

questions.notes: Card correct when polar deserts count: Antarctica is mainly a polar desert holding about 70% of the world's freshwater reserves (Wikipedia: Antarctica), and Wikipedia's Desert article calls it the world's largest cold desert; at ~14 million km² it is larger than the Sahara (~9 million km²), the largest hot desert.
